properties.content: Question: humira induced lupus symptoms Answer: Humira, a TNF inhibitor, can sometimes induce symptoms similar to lupus, known as drug-induced lupus erythematosus (DIL). Common symptoms include joint pain, muscle pain, fatigue, fever, and skin rashes. These symptoms can be mild or more severe, and may include inflammation around the lungs or heart (serositis). If you experience these symptoms while taking Humira, it's important to consult with your doctor for proper diagnosis and management, as discontinuing Humira can often resolve the symptoms. More detailed information:: - Symptoms: While lupus symptoms can vary, drug-induced lupus can manifest with a range of issues. Common signs include: - Diagnosis: Diagnosis of drug-induced lupus can be challenging as symptoms may overlap with other conditions. A healthcare provider will typically take a detailed medical history, perform a physical exam, and order specific blood tests, such as ANA (antinuclear antibody) testing, to help determine if the symptoms are related to Humira. - Treatment: The primary treatment for Humira-induced lupus is to stop or reduce the dosage of Humira. In many cases, symptoms will subside after the medication is discontinued. In more severe cases, your doctor may prescribe corticosteroids or other medications to manage the symptoms.
